newsitem.title: USA: U.S. commerce chief to lead mission to Canada.
newsitem.headline: U.S. commerce chief to lead mission to Canada.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Commerce William Daley said Friday he will lead a group of executives from small and medium-sized firms on a trade mission to Canada.
Daley said the mission would highlight the trade opportunities available for such companies, which represent a major source of new jobs in the U.S. economy.

"Some of the most creative thinking and innovative skills are at work in small firms," Daley said. "The more we can expose these firms to opportunities around the world, helping them tap into projects and new developments, the more these small firms will grow and create jobs here at home."
Daley said Canada presented good opportunities because it was the United States' largest trading partner and because of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) there are fewer barriers.
Executives from 30 to 35 firms are expected to participate in the August 3-8 mission to Montreal, Ottawa, Toronto and Vancouver, the Commerce Department said.
The United States and Canada traded goods worth more than $370 billion last year, the department said.
